findings.claim: the base-move two-step was structurally unexecutable: the moved-base guard anchored on the base commit (which always predates the move), bricking the bare fence forever, while fence parity applied the pin law retroactively so the old-base push refused on all eight grandfathered commits
the advance task's only pin was degenerate: its RED was the vacuous-range refusal and its GREEN audits the self-authorizing commit — verified in form, disclosed in substance
findings.justification: a base move has no external test to pin; the pin discriminates the fence's empty-versus-nonempty range semantics, which is the change's actual behavior. Disclosed in the register.

findings.claim: the fence-surface change landed while its authorizing record sat mid-flight and its register was uncommitted — a transient bearer-citation window
commit timestamps are neutral by policy while event timestamps are honest session time: the artifact reads as backdating unless the policy is known
findings.justification: deliberate commit-timestamp neutrality (the public-history leak discipline) alongside honest event timestamps is standing policy, recorded in two prior registers; the divergence is the audit trail.

findings.claim: the sweep range is client-aimed: prepare defaults to HEAD~1 and nothing ties the pinned span to the task's commit footprint
findings.justification: range-to-commit binding is the registered task-commit binding design (issue #8); until then dispatch discipline plus the pinned-sha swept range is the documented boundary.

findings.claim: the GREEN re-run leaves no durable event: the done transition is trusted computation, not recorded evidence
findings.justification: the transition event plus the git history of the record is the evidence; a recorded green-run event would be more client-writable prose, not stronger evidence.

findings.claim: WIRING's PR claim met an unconditional bare CI step
